positions.pos: Each element gets a land after Magic's: metal is the cave (swamp), fire a volcanic mountain, earth open plains with a barrow, water an island, wood an old forest. Fire takes the mountain and earth the plains so the two do not share one. This stands unless you flip it.
positions.why: His mapping of 14 October, with earth as plains because mountain is fire's. Sheet: council/callsheets/element-settings.md.

positions.pos: Water is an island outside and a lagoon inside, entered by wading, with the reef as the lagoon's floor. This stands unless you flip it.
positions.why: He offered reef or lagoon and settled on island; the lagoon is the one that has a floor and a still surface to stand on, and the reef rides under it.

positions.pos: Every land uses the WAVE room's seven stretches and the hall of the six unchanged. Only the dressing changes: light, fog, ground and pieces. This stands unless you flip it.
positions.why: The look table (STEP_LOOK, FACE_LOOK) already works this way, so one skeleton serves five lands and nothing is rebuilt per element.

positions.pos: The Chapter 1 demo keeps the cave as its only setting. The other four lands come after it. This stands unless you flip it.
positions.why: The Kickstarter gate is a working gamified Chapter 1 that ends in the cave (chapter1-demo.md); adding lands first spends the demo's time on breadth.

positions.pos: Wood is the first land built after the demo gate, from one paragraph through room-from-text, ahead of fire, earth and water. This stands unless you flip it.
positions.why: The forest has the most already made: procgen roots and mushrooms, the greenery picks and the grass clump. It is the cheapest test of whether a land reads as a land.
